title: Majestic: The Quiet King Move Before Mate
summary: Prepare a checking pawn break, then use the king to turn the opponent’s promotion into a mating trap.

nodes.question: Can the bishop stop the a-pawn in time?
nodes.explanation: Begin after ...Kxc6: White Ka6/Bg5/c2/d2 faces Kc6/a3/d4. The knight sacrifice has removed the defender of d4, but Black can return to defend it.

nodes.question: The pawn is ready to promote. Why move the king?
nodes.explanation: After c4+ ...Kc5, White must improve the king before the bishop can deliver the final mating check.

branches.title: Prepare the break, then play the quiet king move
commentary: Begin after ...Kxc6: White Ka6/Bg5/c2/d2 faces Kc6/a3/d4. The knight sacrifice has removed the defender of d4, but Black can return to defend it.
Bf6 attacks d4 along e5 and prepares access to the promotion diagonal.
Kd5 returns to defend d4, so Bxd4 would allow the king to capture the bishop.
d3 prepares c4 with check and protects the bishop’s future c3 square.
a2 moves one step from promotion, but gives White the checking tempo.
c4+ is a two-square pawn move with check. Black may capture en passant, but that opens the bishop’s diagonal.
Kc5 declines en passant and keeps d4 defended.
Kb7 is the quiet king move. It covers b6/c6 and prepares Be7 mate if the pawn promotes.
a1=Q promotes, but the queen on a1 cannot prevent the immediate mating check.
Be7# is mate. The bishop checks c5 through d6 and also covers b4; Kb7 covers b6/c6, c4 controls b5/d5, d3 protects c4, and Black’s own pawn blocks d4.
branches.explanation: Be7# is mate. The bishop checks c5 through d6 and also covers b4; Kb7 covers b6/c6, c4 controls b5/d5, d3 protects c4, and Black’s own pawn blocks d4.

branches.title: En passant opens the bishop’s route
commentary: Begin after ...Kxc6: White Ka6/Bg5/c2/d2 faces Kc6/a3/d4. The knight sacrifice has removed the defender of d4, but Black can return to defend it.
Bf6 prepares the promotion diagonal.
Kd5 defends d4 for the moment.
d3 supports c4 and the future bishop landing square c3.
a2 threatens promotion.
c4+ forces an answer and offers en passant.
dxc3 en passant removes c4 but vacates d4, opening f6-e5-d4-c3.
Bxc3 removes the pawn and controls a1 through b2. The bishop is protected by d3, and the exact remaining ending is winning for White.
branches.explanation: Bxc3 removes the pawn and controls a1 through b2. The bishop is protected by d3, and the exact remaining ending is winning for White.

branches.title: Independent king retreat permits the bishop capture
commentary: Compare a legal king retreat instead of the source’s promotion.
Kb7 creates the mating threat.
Kd6 avoids immediate pawn promotion but stops defending d4. This is an independently selected representative reply.
Bxd4 removes the blockader and controls a1. The bishop is protected by c4, and the exact position is winning for White.

branches.title: Independent immediate capture loses the bishop
commentary: Begin after ...Kxc6: White Ka6/Bg5/c2/d2 faces Kc6/a3/d4. The knight sacrifice has removed the defender of d4, but Black can return to defend it.
Bf6 correctly prepares access to d4.
Kd5 defends d4 with the king.
Bxd4 is premature: White has not arranged c4 to protect the bishop.
Kxd4 captures the unsupported bishop. The exact pawn ending is checked rather than judged solely from material.

exercises.prompt: Why is Kb7 useful when a pawn is about to promote?
exercises.answer: It takes away b6 and c6, turning Be7 into mate after promotion. The immediate threat is to the king rather than the new queen.
The break comes with check; if Black captures en passant, the bishop reaches c3 and d3 protects it while it controls a1.

startContext: Begin after ...Kxc6 at 43s, a supported seven-piece diagram. The earlier eight-piece Nc6 sacrifice remains source context. The d3/c4 checking break, legal en passant defense, quiet Kb7 and promotion mate are checked. The transcript’s reference to A3 preparing c4 is corrected to the visible d3; other king/capture comparisons are independently selected. This is a closely related version of Most Majestic Game (zpX6pvMJhto): the bishop begins on g5 here rather than h4, and both reach the same Bf6 continuation. This version has its own reviewed source diagrams and checked selected branches.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.

sourceCorrections.claim: The captions later refer to A3 as the move preparing c4.
sourceCorrections.correction: The saved board and the earlier narration show d2-d3. That pawn protects the bishop on c3 after en passant.
